answer: An agent network can require each new vertex to earn endorsements from several long-lived, independently bonded peers before it can influence shared decisions. Endorsement weight decays with time, so a newcomer must build a track record across a meaningful horizon rather than buy one burst of approval. Peers lose part of their bond if they endorse accounts later caught coordinating fraud. A sybil operator must therefore acquire many costly bonds and persuade trusted peers to risk theirs, creating a financial ridge that makes fake identities expensive to scale.
